system_metadata.core_domain: Team Alignment, Psychological Safety, Project Governance, Conflict Resolution

visual_grounding_analogies.name: The Blindfolded Team (Walking in the Dark)
visual_grounding_analogies.description: Depicts team members wearing blindfolds, stumbling around a room with chairs and obstacles, asking 'Does anyone understand what we're supposed to do?'. Illustrates complete lack of common ground and mutual awareness.
visual_grounding_analogies.risk: Silent perception gaps where team members assume alignment, resulting in catastrophic coordination surprises, duplicated work, and project failure.
visual_grounding_analogies.action: Forbid jumping into execution or task breakdown until a synchronized Forward Pass is executed and all Joint Objectives & Commitments are explicitly defined.

visual_grounding_analogies.name: The Parachute Cliff Jump (Overoptimism Trap)
visual_grounding_analogies.description: Depicts a team member leaping off a cliff with a parachute that breaks or fails, shouting 'I told you we were going too fast!'.
visual_grounding_analogies.risk: Launching projects based on unexamined optimism without systematically identifying latent risks, dependencies, and missing resources.
visual_grounding_analogies.action: Enforce a mandatory Backward Pass on every plan to systematically transform every identified risk and missing resource into concrete mitigation objectives or explicit commitments.

visual_grounding_analogies.name: The Resource Avalanche (Resource Fistfight)
visual_grounding_analogies.description: Depicts team members wrestling on the floor surrounded by falling money and gear, screaming 'I lack resources!'.
visual_grounding_analogies.risk: Committing to objectives without explicit, allocated resources (time, budget, human bandwidth, tools), causing workflows to freeze and interpersonal friction to spike.
visual_grounding_analogies.action: Enforce explicit resource estimation and allocation per objective. If a resource cannot be guaranteed, the linked Joint Objective must be modified or removed.

visual_grounding_analogies.name: The Superhero Leader (Micromanagement / Exhaustion Trap)
visual_grounding_analogies.description: Depicts an exhausted leader trying to pull, direct, and carry all team members through a door single-handedly.
visual_grounding_analogies.risk: Leader bottlenecking, team disengagement, lack of psychological ownership, and eventual leader burnout.
visual_grounding_analogies.action: Enforce 'Aligned Autonomy': Leadership sets the 'What & Why' (Mission/Objectives), while team members self-organize and define the 'How' during the Forward and Backward Passes.

visual_grounding_analogies.name: The Prenup Paradox (Overly Punitive Contract)
visual_grounding_analogies.description: Depicts a couple entering a marriage agreement while obsessed with divorce penalties, breaking the cooperative atmosphere.
visual_grounding_analogies.risk: Over-indexing on harsh penalties in team agreements destroys trust and triggers paranoia from day one.
visual_grounding_analogies.action: Frame Team Contracts around shared conventions, positive behaviors, and fair decision processes rather than legalistic sanctions. Address breaches through diplomatic learning conversations.

risk_exposure_formula.rule: High-exposure risks must be prioritized during the Backward Pass and converted into actionable Joint Objectives.

scoring_threshold.interpretation: Scores < 40 indicate high psychological danger, requiring immediate Team Contract interventions.

zones.green_zone: Top 1/3 of slider (Clear, Explicit, Available, Under Control). High probability of success.
zones.red_zone: Bottom 2/3 of slider (Unclear, Implicit, Missing, Underestimated). High probability of failure.

aligned_autonomy_formula.rule: Autonomy cannot exist without alignment. High alignment + high clarity = max team speed.

header.mission: Challenging, audacious, unique, or fun statement framed as [Goal + Benefit] or 'How might we...?'
header.period: Exact timeframe, duration, or deadline (e.g., '2 weeks', 'Q3', 'By Oct 15')

columns: Joint Objectives (What do we intend to achieve together?)
Joint Commitments (Who will do what with whom?)
Joint Resources (What resources do we need?)
Joint Risks (What can prevent us from succeeding?)

sections.in: Accepted behaviors, team values, communication rules, meeting norms, decision-making protocols.
sections.out: Unacceptable behaviors (lateness, silent disagreement, public criticism, scope creep without discussion).

failure_framing_matrix.complex_operations: Analyze and fix complex failures (system breakdowns).
failure_framing_matrix.innovation_research: Celebrate intelligent failures (hypotheses tested, fast learning).

traps.incomplete_facts: Lack of key detail -> 'Who? What? When? Where? Could you be more precise?'
traps.assumptions: Creative causal leaps -> 'What makes you think so? How do you know X causes Y?'
traps.generalizations: Universal rules ('always', 'never') -> 'Always? Never? Everyone? Are you sure?'
traps.limitations: Imaginary constraints ('can't', 'must') -> 'What would happen if...? What prevents us?'
traps.judgments: Subjective value statements ('bad', 'poor') -> 'What criteria tell you that? In what way?'

respect_card.recognition_drivers: Expressing gratitude, acknowledging unique talents, validating contributions.
respect_card.respect_drivers: Using indirect requests ('Would you mind...'), preserving face, giving feedback privately.

nonviolent_requests_schema.structure:
1. Observation: 'When you do [factual action]...'
2. Feeling: 'I feel [emotion]...'
3. Need: 'My need is [core need]...'
4. Request: 'Would you please [concrete action]?'
